metadata.title: ECDSA Algebraic Anomalies Research Knowledge Base
metadata.author: Crypton Systems Lab
metadata.description: Structured knowledge base for research on algebraic anomalies in ECDSA signatures. Designed as machine-readable context for AI agents and research progress tracking.

ecdsa_signing_equation.name: ECDSA Signing Equation
ecdsa_signing_equation.description: The core ECDSA relation: s = (z + r·x) · k⁻¹ mod n, where s is the signature scalar, z is the message hash, r is the x-coordinate of k·G mod n, x is the private key, k is the ephemeral nonce, and n is the curve order.

s_zk.name: s_zk component
s_zk.description: The message-hash-dependent component of the signature: s_zk = z · k⁻¹ mod n. This is the portion of s derived from the hash and nonce, independent of the private key.
s_zk.note: Hidden (non-public) parameter; requires knowledge of k to compute directly.

s_rxk.name: s_rxk component
s_rxk.description: The private-key-dependent component of the signature: s_rxk = r · x · k⁻¹ mod n. This is the portion of s that encodes the private key.
s_rxk.note: Hidden (non-public) parameter. s = s_zk + s_rxk mod n.

s_zr.name: s_zr product
s_zr.description: The product of the two public parameters z and r, computed modulo n.

anomaly_remainder_a.name: Anomaly parameter a
anomaly_remainder_a.description: The modular remainder a = s mod (s_zr - s) mod n, computed when s_zr > s. This value acts as a structural invariant connecting public signature components to hidden decomposition parameters.

factor_ratio_m1.name: Factor ratio m1
factor_ratio_m1.description: The ratio m1 = s_zk / a. When m1 is an integer, the signature falls into class A (if m1=1), B (if m1=m2), or C (otherwise). When m1 is non-integer, the signature falls into class D.

factor_ratio_m2.name: Factor ratio m2
factor_ratio_m2.description: The ratio m2 = (s + s_zr) / s_rxk. Compared with m1 to distinguish anomaly subclasses B and C.

factor_ratio_f.name: Fractional factor ratio f
factor_ratio_f.description: For class D anomalies, f = m1 = s_zk / a is a non-integer rational number. The integer part ⌊f⌋ defines the D-level (D0, D1, D2, ...). The fractional part encodes information about the nonce-key relationship.

anomaly_detection_condition.name: Anomaly detection condition
anomaly_detection_condition.description: An ECDSA transaction exhibits an algebraic anomaly (classes A-D) if and only if s_zr > s AND a > 0 AND a ≠ s AND a ≠ s_zr.

goldbach_condition.name: Goldbach-type condition (class E)
goldbach_condition.description: A signature satisfies the Goldbach condition if s is even, and the absolute difference |s_zk - s_rxk| equals ⌊s/2⌋ + 1 - |s_zk - ⌊s/2⌋| + ⌊s/2⌋ - s_rxk (with appropriate sign handling). E1: when s_zk + s_rxk ≤ s. E2: when s_zk + s_rxk > s, requiring s += n adjustment.

subclasses.E2: s_zk + s_rxk > s (s is adjusted to s + n)

factor_window.name: Factor window for D-anomaly
factor_window.description: For a D-anomaly with fractional ratio f, the factor window defines the integer bounds [N, N+1] where N = ⌊f⌋. The corresponding s_zk search range is [a·N, a·(N+1)]. Special case: if N=0, the range is [1, a].

x_candidate_recovery.name: Private key candidate from s_zk guess
x_candidate_recovery.description: Given a guessed s_zk value and public parameters (s, z, r), the candidate private key is computed as x = z·(s - s_zk) · (r · s_zk)⁻¹ mod n.

A.name: Linear divisibility anomaly

classification_criteria.description: m1 is integer, m1 = 1, m2 is non-integer.

A.interpretation: s_zk = a (exactly), meaning the hidden nonce-hash product equals the anomaly remainder.

recovery.description: Direct analytical recovery: compute k from s_zk = a, then recover x from the signing equation.
steps: s_zk = a · m = a · 1 = a
k = s_zk · z⁻¹ mod n
s_rxk = s - s_zk mod n
x = s_rxk · (r · k)⁻¹ mod n

A.frequency_notes: Rare. ~2465 out of ~99.3M transactions on tiny curve, ~4 out of ~1M on small curve, 0 on large curve at 1M tx.

B.name: Quadratic anomaly

classification_criteria.description: Both m1 and m2 are integers, and m1 equals m2.

B.interpretation: Both factor ratios are integer and equal. This creates a quadratic equation in the multiplier m, solvable via modular discriminant.

recovery.description: Solve a modular quadratic equation for m using discriminant and modular square root. May yield two candidate private keys.
steps: D = s² - 4·a·(s_zr + s) mod n
Compute modular square roots of D mod n
For each root: m = (s + root) · (2·a)⁻¹ mod n
s_zk = a · m mod n
k = s_zk · z⁻¹ mod n
x = (s - s_zk) · (r · k)⁻¹ mod n
latex: x = (s - a \cdot m) \cdot (r \cdot a \cdot m \cdot z^{-1})^{-1} \pmod{n}

B.frequency_notes: Extremely rare. 2 out of ~99.3M transactions on tiny curve, 0 on other curves at tested sample sizes.

C.name: Integer non-equal factor anomaly

classification_criteria.description: m1 is integer (and m1 > 1), but either m2 is non-integer, or m1 ≠ m2.

C.interpretation: s_zk is an integer multiple of a (with multiplier > 1), but the second ratio m2 does not match. No closed-form recovery formula has been derived.

recovery.description: No recovery formula exists yet. Returns '-' in current implementation.

C.frequency_notes: Moderate. ~335K out of ~99.3M on tiny curve, ~580 out of ~1M on small curve, 0 on large curve at 1M tx.

D.name: Fractional factor anomaly

classification_criteria.description: m1 = s_zk / a is a non-integer rational number. The integer part ⌊f⌋ defines the D-level.
conditions: D-level N = integer part of f

D.interpretation: The dominant anomaly class (~98-99% of all detected anomalies). The fractional ratio f encodes structural information about the nonce-key relationship. The D-level N determines the width of the candidate s_zk window.

sublevel_structure.description: D-anomalies are subcategorized by level N = ⌊f⌋. D0, D1, D2 are the most frequent; frequency decays monotonically with increasing N.

recovery.description: No closed-form formula. Recovery via brute-force search within bounded s_zk windows, narrowed by intersecting candidate x-sets across multiple transactions sharing the same private key.
steps: For each transaction i: compute factor window [N_i, N_i+1] from f_i
Compute s_zk range: [a_i · N_i, a_i · (N_i + 1)]
For each s_zk candidate in range: compute x_candidate = z·(s - s_zk)·(r·s_zk)⁻¹ mod n
Build index: x → [s_zk values] for each transaction
Intersect x-candidate sets across all transactions
Common x values are private key candidates

D.frequency_notes: Dominant. ~24.4M out of ~24.75M total anomalies on tiny curve (98.6%). 100% on large curve at 1M tx (no A/B/C/E detected).

E.name: Goldbach-type additive decomposition anomaly

classification_criteria.description: s is even, and s_zk, s_rxk satisfy a specific symmetry condition around s/2 related to Goldbach-type additive decomposition.
conditions: Symmetry condition on |s_zk - s_rxk| relative to s/2

subclasses.E2: s_zk + s_rxk > s → s is adjusted to s + n before checking

E.interpretation: The signature scalar s admits a Goldbach-like decomposition where s_zk and s_rxk are complementary components equidistant (±1) from s/2.

recovery.description: Deterministic recovery by computing two candidate private keys from the half-sum decomposition of s.
steps: If E2: s = s + n
s_half = s // 2
a_val = (s + s_half + 1) // 2
b_val = s - a_val
x1 = recover_case_a(s, z, r, a_val, n, m=1)
x2 = recover_case_a(s, z, r, b_val, n, m=1)
latex: s' = \begin{cases} s & \text{if } s_{zk} + s_{rxk} \leq s \\ s + n & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

E.frequency_notes: Very rare. ~6746 out of ~99.3M on tiny curve, ~12 out of ~1M on small curve, 0 on large/legacy at tested sample sizes.

theorems.name: Anomaly A deterministic recovery
theorems.statement: If an ECDSA signature satisfies the anomaly A condition (s_zr > s, a = s mod (s_zr - s) mod n, a > 0, a ≠ s, a ≠ s_zr, and s_zk / a = 1), then the private key x can be recovered deterministically from the public parameters (s, z, r) and the derived value a.
theorems.proof_sketch: Since m1 = 1, we have s_zk = a. This directly yields k = a · z⁻¹ mod n. Substituting back: x = (s - a) · (r · k)⁻¹ mod n.

theorems.name: Anomaly B quadratic recovery
theorems.statement: If an ECDSA signature satisfies anomaly B conditions (m1 = m2, both integer), then the private key can be recovered by solving the modular quadratic D = s² - 4a·(s_zr + s) mod n, yielding up to two candidate keys.
theorems.proof_sketch: Setting m1 = m2 = m and substituting into the ECDSA equation yields a quadratic in m: a·m² - s·m + (s_zr + s) ≡ 0 (mod n). Solving via the quadratic formula in modular arithmetic recovers m, hence s_zk = a·m, hence k and x.
theorems.note: Yields two candidates; correct x must be verified against the public key.

theorems.name: Anomaly E Goldbach-type recovery
theorems.statement: If an ECDSA signature satisfies the Goldbach-type condition on the additive decomposition of s into s_zk and s_rxk, then two candidate private keys can be computed from the half-sum decomposition.

theorems.name: Anomaly D candidate x formula
theorems.statement: For any guessed value of s_zk, the corresponding candidate private key is x = z·(s - s_zk)·(r·s_zk)⁻¹ mod n. This holds unconditionally and is exact when s_zk matches the true hidden value.
theorems.note: This formula is the mathematical foundation of the cross-transaction intersection algorithm.

hypotheses.name: D-anomaly frequency decay law
hypotheses.statement: The count of D-level N anomalies decays approximately as O(1/N) with increasing level N, for sufficiently large transaction samples.
hypotheses.evidence: Observed monotonic decay across all four curve configurations. D0/D1/D2/D3 counts are approximately equal, then decay begins around D3-D4.
hypotheses.importance: If proven, this constrains the expected search window width for the intersection algorithm.

hypotheses.name: Cross-transaction intersection convergence
hypotheses.statement: Given T ≥ 2 transactions from the same private key, the intersection of candidate x-sets converges to a singleton (the true private key) with probability approaching 1 as T increases, provided the D-levels are bounded.
hypotheses.evidence: Verified on test_small curve with T=4 transactions (find_common_private_key.py demo). Convergence observed in all tested cases.
open_questions: Minimum T required for unique intersection on secp256k1?
How does the D-level distribution affect convergence rate?
Computational complexity scaling with curve order n?

hypotheses.name: Anomaly class C recovery possibility
hypotheses.statement: There may exist a closed-form or polynomial-time recovery formula for class C anomalies where m1 is integer, m1 > 1, but m2 ≠ m1 or m2 is non-integer.
hypotheses.evidence: No formula found yet. Class C frequency is non-trivial on small curves but vanishes on larger curves, suggesting it may be a small-field artifact.
hypotheses.importance: Low priority — may not be relevant for secp256k1.

hypotheses.name: Anomaly detection rate ~25% of transactions
hypotheses.statement: Approximately 25% of all ECDSA transactions (with random nonces) satisfy the anomaly detection condition (s_zr > s, a > 0, a ≠ s, a ≠ s_zr), independent of curve size.
hypotheses.evidence: Consistently observed across all four curves: ~24.75M/99.3M (24.9%) on tiny, ~249K/1M (24.9%) on small, ~250K/1M (25.0%) on large.
hypotheses.importance: Suggests the anomaly detection condition is an intrinsic property of modular arithmetic, not a curve-specific artifact.

algorithms.name: Cross-transaction x-intersection
algorithms.description: Given T ≥ 2 D-anomaly transactions sharing the same private key, find the common x by intersecting bounded candidate sets.
algorithms.input: List of T ECDSATransaction objects, each with (s, z, r, a, f)
algorithms.output: List of (x, [s_zk_per_tx]) tuples where x is a candidate private key

complexity.per_transaction: O(a) candidates per transaction (window width = a)
complexity.brute_force_comparison: Cartesian product would be O(∏ aᵢ), intersection reduces this dramatically

steps: For each tx_i: compute N_i = ⌊f_i⌋, range_i = [a_i·N_i, a_i·(N_i+1)]
Sort transactions by ascending range size
Build base x-index from narrowest range transaction
Iteratively intersect with each subsequent transaction's x-index
Return surviving (x, chain) pairs
Optional: verify x against public key if available

experimental_results.note: On larger curves, only D-anomalies are observed. A, B, C, E appear to be small-field phenomena.
